Independently review the following full setup plan for coverage and fidelity, journey usability, ticket sizing/dependencies, feasibility, domain correctness, privacy and acceptance evidence. Return verdict and findings. No writes.
Plotbook setup proposal. Project is brief-only; no code/manifests/git; name Plotbook, type generic and language TBD pending owner technical choice. No writes yet.
Source brief.md: Background: Riverside garden, 40 plots, about 60 households, seasons March–October. Users: gardeners apply/view/report; coordinator reviews/allocates/waitlists/resolves. First version must: (1) coming-season application up to three preferred plots, (2) coordinator allocation and unallocated applicants FIFO waiting list, (3) own allocation plus season dates, (4) gardener problem reporting/coordinator open queue and resolution, (5) coordinator 40-plot holder grid. Rules: at most one plot per household per season; returning prior-season holders applying before 1 February allocated before new applicants; waiting list strictly first come first served. Constraints: phone use, contacts coordinator-only, large text/plain language. Later excluded: online payments and tool lending. Open questions: sign-in and whether/how new problem reports notify coordinator. Stack unstated. These are the full brief facts, not completion claims.
Source labels: every listed first-version item/rule/constraint = requirement (brief.md respective heading). Sign-in and notification = unresolved decision (Open questions); stack = unresolved missing choice. Payments/tool lending = explicit deferrals (Later). All additional operational choices below = proposals/assumptions.
Milestones: Discovery approved prototype/policy; Foundation persistent access-controlled app/inventory; Applications usable phone application; Allocation complete allocation/waitlist/views; Problems reporting/resolution; Acceptance owner-approved v1. Default p0 Setup retained first.
Every ticket below is pending. Ticket descriptions share source brief.md: First version must, Rules, Constraints; P01/2/3/12/15/16 are proposed enabling work/checkpoints referencing that source and Open questions. No automatic phase-order dependency.
P01 [Discovery] Phone-first prototype and policy examples
blockedBy: none
Outcome: Review phone layouts for application, allocation, reporting and coordinator map. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Annotated screens plus examples for returning priority, cutoff and waiting-list order; excludes production code.
Acceptance: All five journeys shown with large text and plain language; examples name unresolved cutoff timezone, exact season dates, household identification, timestamp ties, duplicate application policy, and contact fields.
Behaviour: Show empty, loading, error and retry states; keyboard and readable text annotations.
Verification: Owner walkthrough of screens and worked examples. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: None; illustrative data only.

P02 [Discovery] Checkpoint: approve journeys, policies and technical approach
blockedBy: P01
Outcome: Owner resolves choices required by implementation. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Review P01 artifact; choose sign-in, household linkage, stack/deployment, season dates and cutoff timezone, ties/duplicate policy; notification choice recorded separately as open if postponed. Excludes invented policy defaults.
Acceptance: Question: Does the owner approve the screens and record each core policy/technical choice? Only completed decisions release dependent work.
Behaviour: Unanswered core decisions leave this checkpoint open.
Verification: Decision record references reviewed artifact and explicit owner answers. Prerequisites: P01. Assumptions: No stack or authentication provider chosen.

P03 [Foundation] Establish application, storage and verification tooling
blockedBy: P02
Outcome: Provide a runnable foundation for booking and problem reporting. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Approved stack scaffold, persistent storage/migrations, test/build/dev commands, environment configuration, restart/recovery and backup/restore procedure; excludes product features.
Acceptance: App runs locally, persists sample data across restart, restores a sample backup, and exposes documented verification commands.
Behaviour: Configuration errors give actionable diagnostics without secrets.
Verification: Smoke test, persistence/restore exercise and manifest inspection. Prerequisites: P02. Assumptions: Hosting choices from P02.

P04 [Foundation] Gardener and coordinator access with household isolation
blockedBy: P03
Outcome: Gardeners access their household records; coordinator manages the garden. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Chosen sign-in/recovery, coordinator provisioning, household linkage and contact visibility; excludes public household directory.
Acceptance: Gardener cannot read other households or coordinator-only contacts through UI or direct requests; coordinator can access required contacts; access revoked on sign-out.
Behaviour: Accessible sign-in errors and recovery; deny missing/invalid permissions server-side.
Verification: Role/household access matrix tests including unauthenticated and direct-request attempts. Prerequisites: P03. Assumptions: Household/contact policy from P02.

P05 [Foundation] Manage seasons, 40 plots and previous-season holdings
blockedBy: P03
Outcome: Coordinator maintains inventory and reliable returning-gardener evidence. from brief.md as above.
Scope: 40 stable plot identifiers, approved season dates, prior holdings entry/import and validation; excludes map UI.
Acceptance: Exactly 40 unique plots are usable per season; dates validate; prior holdings identify returning households without fabricated history.
Behaviour: Invalid or conflicting prior records rejected with correction guidance; safe repeated imports if import selected.
Verification: Fixtures and tests for seasons, duplicates and prior-season lookup. Prerequisites: P03. Assumptions: Coordinator supplies real inventory/history; no real contacts in fixtures.

P06 [Applications] Submit a seasonal application with plot preferences
blockedBy: P04, P05
Outcome: Gardener applies for the coming season with up to three preferred plots. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Phone application form, preferred-plot validation, authoritative received timestamp and confirmation; excludes allocation.
Acceptance: Valid application persists for household/season with 0–3 distinct valid preferences; duplicate policy follows P02; successful retry cannot create duplicates.
Behaviour: Accessible validation, empty plot state, saving state, recoverable failure and preserved input.
Verification: End-to-end phone application and boundary/retry tests. Prerequisites: P04, P05. Assumptions: Zero preferences permitted as proposed interpretation of 'up to three', subject to P02.

P07 [Allocation] Review applications and enforce returning priority
blockedBy: P06
Outcome: Coordinator reviews applications with correct allocation eligibility. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Eligibility from prior holdings and application timestamp before 1 February; readable priority reasons; excludes waiting-list ranking.
Acceptance: Qualifying returners must be processed before new applicants; cutoff boundary and late-returner treatment follow owner ruling; arbitrary UI sort cannot bypass rule.
Behaviour: Missing history flagged for correction; no silent priority guess.
Verification: Table-driven prior-season and cutoff boundary tests plus coordinator walkthrough. Prerequisites: P06. Assumptions: Allocation priority and waiting-list FIFO are distinct rules.

P08 [Allocation] Allocate one plot per household per season
blockedBy: P07
Outcome: Coordinator assigns available plots to eligible applications. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Manual assignment, conflict checks and persistent allocation; excludes automatic optimisation and new reassignment/cancellation workflows.
Acceptance: At most one plot per household and, as proposed physical constraint, one holder per plot per season; allocation honours P07; preference choice remains coordinator-controlled.
Behaviour: Atomic conflict rejection, stale-screen refresh, safe retry, clear success/failure.
Verification: Concurrent same-household/same-plot tests; failure rollback and rule-bypass tests. Prerequisites: P07. Assumptions: One holder per plot is a labelled assumption for P02 approval; preferences are requests, not guarantees.

P09 [Allocation] Maintain the chronological waiting list
blockedBy: P08
Outcome: Coordinator places unallocated applicants on a FIFO waiting list and allocates vacancies in order. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Explicit queue placement, original application timestamp ordering, approved tie-break, removal on allocation and head-first vacancy assignment; excludes discretionary reordering.
Acceptance: Only unallocated households are queued; placement time never changes application order; repeated actions do not duplicate entries; vacancy allocation cannot skip the first eligible queued applicant.
Behaviour: Show empty queue and allocation conflicts; retain position on failed assignment.
Verification: Mixed returning/new fixtures, equal timestamps, retries and concurrent vacancy assignment. Prerequisites: P08. Assumptions: Conflict or exception policy requiring skipping remains an owner decision; no priority boost on waiting list.

P10 [Allocation] Show gardener allocation and season dates
blockedBy: P04, P08
Outcome: Gardener sees their allocated plot and the season dates. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Own-household view and pending/unallocated states; excludes other households' data.
Acceptance: Correct plot and exact approved season dates displayed; no allocation represented clearly.
Behaviour: Large text, phone layout, loading/retry states and permission handling.
Verification: Role isolation and phone end-to-end tests across allocated and unallocated states. Prerequisites: P04, P08. Assumptions: No waiting-position disclosure unless separately approved.

P11 [Allocation] Show coordinator grid of all 40 plots
blockedBy: P04, P05, P08
Outcome: Coordinator sees who holds each plot in a grid. from brief.md as above.
Scope: 40 labelled cells, holder/unallocated state and accessible narrow-screen equivalent; excludes geographic survey map.
Acceptance: All 40 plots appear exactly once; holders match committed allocations; accessible status is not colour-only; gardener role denied.
Behaviour: Loading, empty and stale/error states; keyboard navigation and large readable text.
Verification: Grid/data consistency, coordinator-only request checks and phone/keyboard inspection. Prerequisites: P04, P05, P08. Assumptions: Grid is schematic as specified.

P12 [Allocation] Checkpoint: demonstrate seasonal allocation
blockedBy: P09, P10, P11
Outcome: Owner validates application-to-allocation and queue workflows. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Review working phone application, priority examples, assignment, FIFO queue, own allocation and grid; excludes problem-reporting signoff.
Acceptance: Criteria: owner observes the three domain rules and contact privacy on representative synthetic households.
Behaviour: Failures remain recorded and checkpoint stays open.
Verification: Owner demonstration with preserved acceptance record. Prerequisites: P09, P10, P11. Assumptions: Checkpoint is an ordinary ticket; tooling does not enforce owner-only closure.

P13 [Problems] Report a problem for the household's plot
blockedBy: P04, P10
Outcome: Gardener reports a broken tap or similar problem tied to their plot. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Plain-text problem form and persisted open report with household/plot association; excludes photos, chat and notifications pending decision.
Acceptance: Only an allocated household can report against its own plot; valid report appears in coordinator queue; retry is duplicate-safe.
Behaviour: Clear no-plot state, required-description validation, confirmation and recoverable saving failure.
Verification: Phone submission, unauthorised plot substitution and retry tests. Prerequisites: P04, P10. Assumptions: Plain text is proposed minimum; no unnecessary personal data.

P14 [Problems] Review and resolve reported problems
blockedBy: P13
Outcome: Coordinator sees open problems and marks them resolved. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Open-problem queue, details and persisted resolution state; excludes notification delivery until owner decides.
Acceptance: All open reports visible to coordinator; resolving removes item from open queue while preserving report; repeated resolution safe; gardener cannot resolve.
Behaviour: Accessible empty/loading/error states; conflicts and retries handled.
Verification: Report-to-resolution end-to-end test and role/concurrency tests. Prerequisites: P13. Assumptions: No notification provider or channel assumed.

P15 [Problems] Checkpoint: decide problem-report notifications
blockedBy: P01
Outcome: Owner decides whether/how coordinator learns about new reports. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Review problem-flow prototype and an in-app-only versus delivery decision; excludes implementation of an unchosen channel.
Acceptance: Question: Is in-app queue sufficient, or is a named notification channel required for v1? Required delivery triggers a scoped reviewed plan amendment before acceptance.
Behaviour: Decision may remain open without blocking unrelated booking/reporting work.
Verification: Explicit recorded owner decision; any required delivery ticket becomes a final-acceptance prerequisite. Prerequisites: P01. Assumptions: No automatic channel recommendation or outbound messaging.

P16 [Acceptance] Checkpoint: accept first-version Plotbook
blockedBy: P12, P14, P15
Outcome: Owner accepts all five journeys against the brief. from brief.md as above.
Scope: Phone usability, large text/plain language, privacy, domain invariants, restart/recovery and operational walkthrough; excludes payments and tool lending.
Acceptance: Criteria: all five brief journeys demonstrated; 40-plot grid correct; household limit/returner cutoff/FIFO tests pass; access checks pass; any required notification amendment complete.
Behaviour: Failure recovery and accessible validation demonstrated; open mandatory defects prevent acceptance.
Verification: Owner demonstration plus test/build/verification evidence once tooling established. Prerequisites: P12, P14, P15. Assumptions: No invented performance thresholds or completed capability claims.
Coverage map: Must1 P06; Must2 P07 P08 P09; Must3 P10; Must4 P13 P14; Must5 P11; household limit P08; returner cutoff P05 P07 P08; FIFO P09; phone/simple text P01 P06 P10 P11 P13 P16; contact privacy P04 P10 P11 P13 P14 P16. Exact dates/history P02 P05; sign-in P02 P04; notifications P15 then scope amendment if needed. Payments/tool lending deferred explicitly.
Governance: create AGENTS.md product, v1 boundary, planned architecture/entities, unresolved choices and testing strategy; RULES.md domain constraints, privacy, atomic/idempotent transitions, tests-first core logic; REVIEW.md installed template verbatim. Preview available. Git init and .gitignore .story/snapshots/, .story/sessions/, .story/status.json. No GitHub import.
Quality Full pipeline proposed due allocation workflows/business rules. No commands established: WRITE_TESTS/TEST/BUILD/VERIFY explicitly disabled until P03 establishes stack commands. Proposed commands: each TBD after P02 stack choice/P03 manifests; VERIFY dev start/readiness also TBD and applicability checked. No install/test/build/server execution during setup.
Checkpoint limitation: ordinary tickets, no enforced owner gate. Open decisions remain visible and affected work blocked. Immediately actionable: P01 prototype/policy examples only.
Review requested before presenting approval; report supported verdict plus findings; do not claim setup done.
STORYBLOQ_PLAN"
